text:
anya: Quick heads-up — I'm opening a proposal to coalesce retention windows for analytics metrics to reduce index/partition churn and long-tail query cost. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/analytics/pull/874.

mike: can you sketch the scope? which tables/fields are affected?

anya: Main target is metrics.time_buckets and metric_events. Today we keep 1h/6h/24h variants and a separate 'sparse' table for low-cardinality routes. Idea: collapse 1h and 6h into a single 6h window for low-cardinality routes, and add a compact_index that drops rarely-used attributes.

jun: FYI we've seen index sizes double on metrics indexes over last 6 weeks after the product tagging change — p99 write latency spike correlates with increased index IO. Numbers in /shared/ops/metrics_growth.csv.

oliver: proposed safe migration plan:
1) create compact index concurrently (no blocking writes)
2) dual-write new compact rows while keeping old data untouched
3) run a sampling read-rewrite in canary that prefers compact index via planner_hint
4) backfill compact rows for last 30d in low-traffic segments
5) flip read path to prefer compact index, keep old as fallback
6) remove old index after 90d and monitoring windows look good

leah: major ask — dashboard owners need zero-visible regressions. Any change to cardinality or retention must upstream to billing/quotas so invoices don't jump. Also ensure retention metadata surfaces in Console so customers see expected window.

mike: how do we detect regressions automatically? could we run synthetic dashboard queries and compare p95/p99 and row counts pre/post?

anya: yes — plan is to run nightly synthetic query jobs that compare results between old and compact index for a sample of routes. Acceptance = identical counts ±1% and explain plan shows index usage.

oliver: SQL I plan to use for the compact index (create concurrently):
```sql
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY metrics_compact_idx ON metric_events (route_id, metric_name, bucket)
WHERE attributes_compressed = true;
```
Then use this planner hint for canary reads:
```sql
SET local enable_seqscan = off; -- encourage index usage for test only
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) SELECT count(*) FROM metric_events WHERE route_id = 'r_123' AND bucket >= '2026-03-01';
```
Sample explain we got on canary: "Index Scan using metrics_compact_idx on metric_events  (cost=0.29..123.45) (actual time=1.2..4.8 rows=1200 loops=1)"

jun: backfill cost estimate? we should avoid touching hot partitions. Maybe use per-route pacing and skip routes with >10k writes/day.

leah: also need a migration toggle in Console so SRE/customers can roll back per-tenant if they see anomalies. UX: a simple flag on route settings and an audit log entry.

anya: agreed. SRE runbook items: rollout in stages (dev -> staging -> canary 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%), monitor metrics: query p95/p99, attribution mismatches, invoices delta, and index bloat. Abort criteria listed in PR description.

mike: volunteers for first canary window? I'll take monitoring dashboards and set up synthetic job harness. :raised_hands:

oliver: I'll own the backfill tool and pacing. Will add safety checks to skip hot routes and emit backfill progress to /infra/backfills.

jun: I'll run a pre-flight run on the sample dataset and post results in this thread by EOD.

deploy-bot: PR #874 has been deployed to canary (cluster: canary-03). Status: succeeded.

anya: Awesome. Next steps: mike to create synthetic query set, oliver to open backfill tool PR, leah to draft Console toggle spec, and jun to run pre-flight. We'll reconvene after the first canary run. :thumbsup:
